subtopics.title: The Intrusion Family — Batholith to Sill

questions.question: A CONCORDANT intrusion is one that:
options: Squeezes BETWEEN the strata, respecting the layering — like a sill, laccolith or lopolith

questions.question: A batholith is:
options: A thin horizontal sheet between strata
An enormous, deep-seated, discordant granite mass, tens to hundreds of kilometres across, with no known floor
A vertical wall in a crack

questions.question: The laccolith and lopolith differ in that:
options: The laccolith is discordant and the lopolith concordant
The lopolith arches the roof upward
The laccolith ARCHES the overlying strata up into a mushroom blister, while the heavy lopolith SAGS the strata beneath it into a saucer

questions.question: The world's largest lopolith, source of most of the planet's platinum, is:
options: The BUSHVELD IGNEOUS COMPLEX north of Pretoria

subtopics.title: From Buried Intrusion to Standing Landform

questions.question: A buried intrusion becomes a landform through:
options: Stripping of the cover by erosion, after which the harder igneous rock RESISTS while the country rock wastes away

questions.question: A resistant dyke exposed in softer country rock forms:
options: A long, narrow, WALL-like ridge marching straight across country

questions.question: An exposed resistant sill typically appears as:
options: A vertical wall cutting across valleys
A horizontal cliff band at one level, a hard cap on a mesa, or the lip of a waterfall

questions.question: On a map, a dyke betrays itself as:
options: A contour-hugging cliff line at constant height
A dead-straight narrow ridge that ignores the drainage pattern

questions.question: Pressure release, or unloading, happens when:
options: Erosion strips the overburden, the pressure on the deep granite drops, and the rock expands slightly
Rain adds weight to the granite

questions.question: Sheet joints are:
options: Curved cracks PARALLEL to the land surface, wrapped around the granite like onion layers, formed by expansion
Cracks made by plant roots only

questions.question: Exfoliation makes a granite dome MORE rounded because:
options: Each curved sheet that peels away exposes a fresh, smoother curved surface beneath — the dome renews its own shape
Rivers carve it into a circle

questions.question: Textbook examples of granite dome scenery include:
options: The Three Sisters and the Fish River Canyon
Paarl Mountain's domes and the whalebacked hills of the Matopos

questions.question: In the two-stage theory of tor formation, the FIRST stage is:
options: Deep chemical weathering underground, where water along the joints rots each block into a rounded corestone wrapped in grus
Boulders rolling downhill into a pile

questions.question: Corners of a jointed granite block round off fastest because they are:
options: Attacked by weathering from THREE sides at once, while edges get two and faces only one

questions.question: The tor becomes visible when:
options: Erosion strips away the soft grus, leaving the hard corestones freestanding in their original stacked positions
People pile the boulders for landmarks

questions.question: The joint-spacing rule says:
options: Close joints give domes, wide joints give tors
Joint spacing has no effect on landforms
Joints only occur in sedimentary rock
WIDELY spaced joints leave huge blocks that weather into domes, while CLOSELY spaced joints give small blocks that become corestones and tors

subtopics.title: The Dough That Never Reached the Surface

questions.question: In the bakery picture, the whole sack of dough with no known bottom is:
The bun that puffed its ceiling up and the saucer that sagged its floor are:
The buried wall and the buried shelf are:
options: DYKE — vertical, cutting the layers — and SILL — horizontal, lying with the layers
Two names for the same thing

questions.question: The single test that sorts all five intrusions is:
options: Does the shape LIE WITH the layers — concordant — or CUT ACROSS them — discordant

questions.question: The squashed taxi passenger stands for:
options: Granite compressed under kilometres of overlying rock, which expands slightly once erosion unloads the weight

questions.question: The expanding granite cracks:
options: In curved shells parallel to the surface, layered like an onion
Not at all — granite cannot crack

questions.question: Exfoliation polishes the mountain into a dome rather than rubble because:
options: The rock melts smooth in the sun
Wind carries the fragments away instantly
Curved shells can only shed into curves — each peeled slab leaves a smoother, rounder surface beneath

subtopics.title: The Sugar-Cube Trick Behind Every Tor

questions.question: In the sugar-cube picture, the tea seeping along the gaps stands for:
options: Groundwater creeping along the JOINTS and chemically rotting each block from every crack inward

questions.question: Each buried block becomes:
options: A rounded CORESTONE sitting in its own crumbly rot, the grus

questions.question: A tor is best described as:
options: A pile built up by rockfalls from above
A stack of survivors LEFT BEHIND when erosion stripped the rotten grus from around the corestones
Boulders carried and dumped by a river

questions.question: One granite koppie can carry both a dome and tors because:
options: Domes turn into tors at night
Tors grow on top of domes
Joint spacing varies across the hill — wide spacing polishes into dome, close spacing rots into corestone stacks
